questions.text: A non-pipelined processor executes an instruction in 12 ns. The same design is split into a 4-stage pipeline with stage delays 3, 4, 2 and 3 ns, plus a 1 ns latch delay per stage. What is the speedup for a very large number of instructions, rounded to two decimals?
questions.explain: Pipeline clock period is set by the slowest stage plus latch: 4 + 1 = 5 ns. Asymptotic speedup = 12 / 5 = 2.4.

questions.text: A byte-addressable machine has 32-bit addresses, a 16 KB 4-way set-associative cache and 32-byte blocks. How many bits are used for the tag?
questions.explain: Blocks = 16384 / 32 = 512. Sets = 512 / 4 = 128, needing 7 index bits. Block offset needs 5 bits. Tag = 32 - 7 - 5 = 20 bits.

questions.text: Cache access takes 2 ns, main memory access takes 100 ns, and the hit ratio is 0.95. On a miss the block is fetched from memory and then read from the cache. What is the average memory access time in nanoseconds?
Which pipeline hazard is caused by an instruction needing a result that a still-executing earlier instruction has not yet produced?
questions.explain: That is a data hazard, specifically read-after-write. Structural hazards come from resource conflicts and control hazards from branches.

questions.text: Which addressing mode is most suitable for implementing a pointer dereference where the address itself is held in memory?
questions.explain: Memory indirect fetches an address from a memory location and then accesses that address, which is exactly a dereference of a stored pointer.

questions.text: A memory system uses 4-way low-order interleaving with a module access time of 40 ns and a bus transfer time of 10 ns per word. How long in nanoseconds does it take to read 4 consecutive words once the first access has been initiated?
questions.explain: All four modules start in a staggered pipeline. First word is available after 40 ns, and the remaining three arrive one bus cycle apart: 40 + 3 x 10 = 70 ns.

questions.text: What is the main advantage of DMA over interrupt-driven I/O for a large block transfer?
options: The device does not need a controller
The CPU is not involved per word transferred
It removes the need for buses
questions.explain: DMA moves the whole block without CPU involvement per word, raising a single interrupt at completion. Interrupt-driven I/O would interrupt for each word.

questions.text: Compared with a hardwired control unit, a microprogrammed control unit is generally:
options: Both faster and easier to modify
questions.explain: Microprogramming stores control signals in a control memory, which costs a lookup per step but lets the instruction set be changed by rewriting microcode rather than redesigning logic.
